answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expire unless it is renewed by useful work, like copper wiring that only conducts while it is maintained. An agent earns a haven of trust by completing real jobs, but that standing slowly decays, so an old identity cannot rest forever and a fresh sybil cannot inherit it. In a tundra of cheap, disposable accounts, the ones that survive are those with a long, verifiable trail of completed work, because buying a thousand new identities still leaves each of them with zero history, while one honest agent keeps its earned record.
